READ-ONLY AUDIT. Do not edit, create, commit or delete any file in treams-rs; do not run builds or tests. Read code only (grep/sed/cat; python3 with the ast module to parse files is fine, but do not import treams_rs).

Repository: treams-rs, Python package python/treams_rs (treams-rs, which mirrors upstream treams conventions).

Binding rules (read first): plan.md §2 "Principles" (Python package paragraph), §5 "Naming rules" (Python sub-rules); decisions.md owner decision 6. In short:

  • Physics objects (TMatrix, CylindricalTMatrix, SMatrix, ScatteringBlock, Wave, PlaneWave, Cluster, PeriodicResponse, PeriodicWave, Material, framework classes in framework*.py ...): canonical physics members first; treams-named members (xs, cd, changepoltype, modetype, poltype, material, illuminate, add, expand, ...) are one-line delegations grouped at the END of the class under ONE comment. Internal code never calls an alias.
  • Private modules: names imported by other modules have no leading underscore and are listed in a literal all.
  • No function-local imports except FieldOperator -> PhysicsArray.

YOUR SLICE, two parts: A) Leftover aliases: treams-named members that are not a grouped one-line delegation at the end of their class (multi-line bodies, scattered placement, missing grouping comment, duplicated grouping comments), and internal code (anywhere in python/treams_rs) that CALLS or READS an alias instead of the canonical member (e.g. tm.poltype, tm.material, incident.material, x.expand(...), .xs, .modetype on treams-rs objects). Known examples to verify and include if still present: io.py save_hdf5 reading tm.poltype/tm.material; iterative.py SphereCluster.scatter reading incident.material/incident.poltype/incident.expand. B) Private helpers used from outside their module: any from ._x import _name or _x._name access where _name starts with an underscore and is defined in another module (also attribute access like obj._private from another module's code on a different class, if clearly cross-module internal API). Also private modules whose cross-module names lack a literal all (e.g. _framework.py has no all while Constructors is imported elsewhere; _tmatrix.py exports axis_mask/solve_columns without all). Also function-local imports other than the allowed one.

Owner map (first match wins) for each finding:

  • python/treams_rs/{special,coeffs,misc,sw,cw,pw}.py -> P25
  • python/treams_rs/lattice.py -> P27
  • python/treams_rs/{ebcm,io,iterative,operators,_operators,_operator_objects,_array,_bases,_lattice,_material,_validation,_polarization,_modes}.py -> P28
  • python/treams_rs/{_tmatrix,_smatrix,_waves,_cluster,_periodic,_results,_upstream,init,diff}.py -> P30
  • python/treams_rs/{advect,jax,torch,testing,_records}.py, python/treams_rs/_framework*.py, python/treams_rs/_native.pyi -> P32
  • otherwise -> none (name the file) Mark each finding's kind: "code change" (P25-P32 are docstring packages, so the lead must judge whether a code change fits) or "docstring/comment only".

Return a concise Markdown section "## Aliases and private helpers" with two tables (A: | File:line | Member or call | Problem | Fix | Owner | Kind |; B: | File:line | Name | Used from | Fix | Owner | Kind |), at most ~50 rows total, verified findings only, most important first.

Aliases and private helpers

I read the code only and changed no files. I parsed every python/treams_rs/*.py with the ast module of python3.13, then checked each hit by hand.

The alias blocks are in good shape. _TMatrix (_tmatrix.py:365), TMatrix (:635), CylindricalTMatrix (:797), SMatrix (_smatrix.py:750), Wave (_waves.py:204) and PlaneWave (_waves.py:460) each have exactly one # treams-compatible names (see treams_rs._upstream.UPSTREAM_MEMBERS) comment. Each block sits at the end of its class, and each alias is a single statement after its docstring. Each block follows the order of its UPSTREAM_MEMBERS entry.

  • The only members after a block are treams-only ones (interaction, latticeinteraction, expandlattice, permute, sphere, cylinder), which is consistent.
  • The SMatrix aliases illuminate, tr, cd, bands_kz and changepoltype delegate to private helpers (_illuminated and so on) rather than to the canonical member. Their signatures and return shapes differ from the canonical ones, so this still reads as a one-line delegation and is not listed below.
  • No framework class (_framework*.py), Cluster, PeriodicResponse or PeriodicWave defines a treams alias. Operations.illuminate uses the diff function's name, so it is canonical.

Checked and clean:

  • The other sibling imports all go through literal __all__ (_records, _lattice, _modes, _polarization, _cluster apart from _DelegatesToLocal, _framework_*).
  • sw.py, cw.py, pw.py, lattice.py and testing.py import non-underscore names and only rename them to _x locally, which is fine.
  • _framework_tmatrix.py's ._backend and ._local() uses, and _lattice.py's private uses, stay within their own module.
  • The only function-local imports are the allowed one at _operator_objects.py:321 and the one at _catalog.py:45 listed above.
